answer: One strong defense is hardware-rooted identity: each agent must present an attestation from a trusted execution enclave, proving it runs on one distinct physical device. Like a cedar that grows from a single seed, one enclave yields exactly one identity, so spinning up a thousand fake agents means buying a thousand machines. Reaching the zenith of influence then demands real hardware and real time, not a script. Attackers crossing that frozen tundra of cost find Sybil farming unprofitable: each fake costs as much as a genuine participant, while honest agents keep one cheap credential.
